solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tube repairer apparently erred at the finish, we hear

indicators.note: something we hear is judged by sound, so the spoken phrase gives a different spelling

parts.note: a runner who ducked the tape at the end of a race would seem to have made a mistake on the line

explanation.surface: An athlete seems to have botched the end of a race, judging by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'ducked tape' out loud and you have the adhesive. 'Apparently' admits that ducking the finishing tape is only a seeming blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Duct tape is the strong cloth-backed adhesive used for patching up hoses, pipes and other tubes.

clue.text: Day One absorbed by some spinning Martian satellite

indicators.note: spinning turns the combined letters round so they read backwards
the numeral for one is soaked up inside the word some

explanation.surface: On day one a spinning moon of Mars is swallowed up by something.
explanation.walkthrough: The D for Day sits outside the reversal; only some-with-I is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Deimos is the smaller and outer of the two moons that orbit the planet Mars.

clue.text: Manage to reduce computer support?

parts.note: to cut is to reduce, as with costs
IT, information technology, is the department that supports computer users

explanation.surface: Can we cope with trimming the tech helpdesk budget?
explanation.definitionFit: To 'cut it' is an idiom for succeeding or being up to a task, as in 'can he cut it?'

clue.text: Obstruct vehicle on rails with short fuse

parts.note: a tram runs along rails in the street

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: to meld is to fuse or blend together

explanation.surface: Someone blocks a tram by shortening its fuse, a piece of rail sabotage.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to hamper or restrain, originally with a net or shackle.

clue.text: Artistic movement promotes minds in torment

indicators.note: minds in torment are twisted and wracked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An art movement advances the cause of tortured minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmodernism is the late-20th-century movement in art, architecture and literature reacting against modernism.

clue.text: Suggestions one thousand are involved in revolutionary swindles

indicators.note: the thousand goes into the middle of the other letters
something revolutionary turns over, so the word for swindles is read backwards

parts.note: K, from kilo, stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand people are caught up in radical cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Smacks are hints or traces of something, as in 'a smack of garlic' or 'it smacks of fraud'.

clue.text: Doctor keeping watch? That's good to hear!

indicators.note: the word for doctor holds the other word inside it

parts.note: lo, as in 'lo and behold', is an old call to look or watch

explanation.surface: A doctor stays on watch, and the patient is relieved to hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something melodic is tuneful, so it is pleasant on the ear.

clue.text: Clothing manufacturer, increasingly friendly, inviting in corporation

indicators.note: the friendlier word welcomes the belly word inside itself

parts.note: cosier means more friendly and snug
corporation is an old humorous word for a pot belly, here a tum

explanation.surface: A clothing firm grows chummier by bringing a big company on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a business, but it is old slang for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, especially for the theatre.

clue.text: Fielder's attempt covering right and left, say

definitions.note: read as 'fielder is', the 's joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the word for attempt wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: a shot is a try or attempt
a left one is an example of a leg

explanation.surface: A cricketer makes a try that covers both the right and left sides.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, short leg is a close fielding position on the leg side, near the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Short leg names a cricket fielding position and so the player stationed there.

clue.text: Popular feature about bridge team is on the way

indicators.note: the word for feature goes round the bridge partnership

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
North and South form one partnership at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A well-loved part of a bridge tournament is on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in transit are being carried and have not yet arrived, so they are en route.

clue.text: Computer retaining much after reprogramming

indicators.note: a reprogrammed system has had its instructions rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A computer keeps a lot of its memory even after being reprogrammed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turing machine is Alan Turing's theoretical model of a general-purpose computing device.

clue.text: Keeps on dropping end of it round — round head of cattle, perhaps

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is lost from the word for keeps on

parts.note: lasts means keeps on or endures

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word it

explanation.surface: A cowboy keeps losing the end of his rope as he circles the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'round' is a verb, as in rounding up cattle; the first gives the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to catch with a looped rope, how a cowhand ropes in a steer.

clue.text: Best work will take reduced time and little hesitation

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: reduced means the word for time is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: um is the brief sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: The finest job will need less time and barely a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable or ideal amount or condition.

clue.text: Fieldwork data from computer ignoring area around capital of Belgium

indicators.note: the remaining letters go round the Belgian initial
ignoring means the area letter is left out

parts.note: a readout is information displayed or printed by a computer

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word Belgium

explanation.surface: Research data about Brussels, minus the surrounding region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fieldwork' suggests research, but it is a military earthwork; 'capital' is a letter, not Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary fortification, the kind of earthwork thrown up in the field.

clue.text: Stormy ocean is ideal source of stuff for coastal city's dish

indicators.note: a stormy sea is churned up, so these letters are tossed about
the source, or first letter, of the word stuff

explanation.surface: A rough sea makes the perfect supply of ingredients for a seaside speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: Salade niçoise is the salad of tuna, olives, egg and anchovies named after Nice on the Riviera.

clue.text: Somehow pro-Venus wanting a light in the heavens

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: Someone who favours Venus somehow still wants a brighter star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' means needing: pro-Venus wants an A added before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is an exploding star that briefly blazes far brighter than normal in the sky.

clue.text: Edited clue — firm but forgiving

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword editor revises a clue, strict yet lenient.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciful means showing compassion and leniency, willing to pardon.

clue.text: Contributor to great pictures in big show certainly satisfied the Queen

parts.note: an expo is a large exhibition
met, as in met a need

explanation.surface: A major art exhibition definitely pleased the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposure meter is a light meter photographers use to set the exposure for a good photograph.

clue.text: Spot intrigue in school

indicators.note: in places the word for intrigue inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: a plot is a scheme or intrigue

explanation.surface: Someone spots scheming going on at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a large irregular mark or stain, a blotchy spot.

clue.text: Paint — moderate source of art?

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or soften

indicators.note: the source, or first letter, of the word art

explanation.surface: Is paint a gentle starting point for art?
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk, used for early panel painting.

clue.text: Enough advanced to replace core component of wages

indicators.note: the lending word goes where the removed letter was, standing in for it
the core of the wages word is its middle letter, which is taken out

parts.note: lent, as money is advanced on loan

explanation.surface: A sufficient loan stands in for the heart of someone's salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty means a sufficient or ample quantity, as in 'that's plenty'.

clue.text: Composer badly taken aback after opening of music omitted

indicators.note: after puts the turned-round letters behind the shortened score
the opening of the word for music is its first letter
omitted means that first letter is left off
taken aback reads the word for badly backwards

explanation.surface: A composer is shocked to find the start of the music missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and composer of concerti grossi.

clue.text: Diverting fuel will keep millions in cars, initially

indicators.note: the fuel word holds the initials inside it
initially takes the first letter of each of the words millions, in and cars

explanation.surface: Fuel subsidies will keep millions of motorists on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverting means amusing or entertaining, which is what comical things are.

clue.text: University blocking mass influence

indicators.note: the university letter sits inside the mass word like a blockage

parts.note: a clot is a lump or mass

explanation.surface: A university obstructs a large group's sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is power or sway, especially political pull.

clue.text: Figurehead runs into various types

indicators.note: into puts the runs letter inside the word for typefaces

parts.note: a font is a set of type in one style and size, so it covers various printed characters
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A leader bumps into all sorts of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A front is a nominal leader or cover behind which others act, like a figurehead.

clue.text: Most significant time to receive care of cat

parts.note: main means chief or most important

indicators.note: the time word takes the care-of letters inside it

parts.note: an eon is a vast age of time

explanation.surface: The key period for getting the cat looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maine coon is a large long-haired breed of domestic cat from the US state of Maine.

clue.text: Hate turning agent about nothing

indicators.note: the machine word goes about the zero letter

parts.note: a lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal

explanation.surface: Someone detests a treacherous spy who is all about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning agent' suggests a double agent; it is a machine tool that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest or feel intense aversion to something.

clue.text: Writer with attempt to capture US lawyer's excessive precision

indicators.note: the pen word captures the lawyer letters inside it

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: An author tries to pin down an American attorney's nitpicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is fussy over-attention to minor details and rules, a fixation on exactness.
